title: 米中露会談 3首脳の思惑が交錯
body: 【ワシントン、北京時事】米中ロ首脳が、史上初となる3カ国首脳会談を開く。既存の国際秩序が揺らぐ中での開催となり、大国の勢力圏分割につながった1945年の米英ソ3首脳による「ヤルタ会談」になぞらえる向きもある。ただ、歴史的な舞台がどれほど内容を伴うかは未知数だ。【ひと目でわかる】米中ロ朝の関係米中は世界1、2位の経済大国。ロシアは言わずと知れた軍事大国で、3カ国とも国連安全保障理事会の常任理事国だ。スウェーデンのストックホルム国際平和研究所（SIPRI）によると、今年1月時点の核弾頭の保有総数はロシアが5420発、米国が5042発、中国が620発で上位3位を占めている。3カ国の首脳が一堂に会する意味は大きく、「米中ロが世界を主導するという図式」（外交関係者）を国際社会に印象付ける可能性がある。トランプ米大統領は、今月3日の米中間選挙で与党共和党が大敗したことから、自身の裁量が大きい外交で「レガシー（政治的遺産）」を残したい意向とされる。ウクライナ侵攻で孤立感が深まるロシアのプーチン大統領には、米中に並ぶ存在感を示す思惑もありそうだ。中国の習近平国家主席にとっても、「大国」としての立場をアピールする機会になる。しかし、米国が議題に挙げる核軍縮や対イラン軍事作戦を巡っては、隔たりがある。トランプ氏は、核戦力を急速に増強する中国を「5、6年でわれわれに追い付くだろう」と警戒。米ロ間の核軍備管理枠組み「新戦略兵器削減条約（新START）」が今年2月に失効したことを受け、3カ国による核軍縮実現に道筋を付けたい考えだ。ロシアは核軍備管理体制の必要性は認めているが、核戦力で米ロに劣る中国は「核軍縮交渉への参加を求められるのは不公平」（中国外務省）と拒否してきた。イラン情勢に関しても、中ロは深入りを避けている。3カ国の利害や思惑は交錯しており、会談の行方は見通せないのが実情だ。

title: ウのNATO加盟で東部撤退 米打診
body: ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアとの和平協議を仲介するアメリカ側から、NATO=北大西洋条約機構への加盟と引き換えに、東部ドンバス地方からの軍の撤退を打診されたと明らかにしました。【写真で見る】「NATO加盟と引き換えにドンバス撤退」アメリカ側がウクライナに初めて打診ウクライナメディアによりますと、ゼレンスキー大統領は13日、アメリカ側から「ウクライナがNATOに加盟する場合、ドンバス地方から軍を撤退させるのか」と問われたことを明らかにしました。ゼレンスキー氏によると、こうした打診を受けるのは初めてで、まだ具体的な情報はないものの、アメリカやNATO加盟国から正式な提案が示された場合には、国民と議論して対応を決める考えを示しました。一方、ロシアはウクライナのNATO加盟を容認しない立場を示しているため、実現性は低いとみられます。ドンバス地方は、ウクライナ東部のドネツク州とルハンシク州からなる地域で、ロシアはドンバス地方全域を掌握するため、侵攻を続けています。ウクライナとロシアの和平協議では東部の領土問題とともに、戦闘終結後の安全の保証などが大きな焦点となっています。

title: 住宅強盗 寝ていた82歳女性が重傷
body: 15日未明、愛知県小牧市の住宅に複数の男が押し入り、住人の高齢女性を棒状のもので殴り逃走しました。警察によりますと、15日午前1時前小牧市小針の住宅で寝ていた女性(82)が電気がついて目を覚ましたところ、そばに3人から4人の男が立っていて「金はないか」と聞かれました。女性は「ない」と答えると、男から背中を棒状のもので殴られ、さらに顔にスプレーのようなものをかけられたということです。その後、男たちはいずれかに逃走しました。女性は肋骨の骨を複数折るなどの重傷ですが、命に別条はないということです。住宅には物色された形跡があり、被害については捜査中ですが、玄関のガラスが割られここから侵入した可能性があるということです。警察は強盗致傷事件として逃げた男の行方を追っています。

title: ラヴ上等「あっすん」容疑者逮捕
body: 無許可で風俗営業店舗を経営したとして、愛知県警は15日、Netflix（ネットフリックス）が配信する「『ラヴ上等』シーズン2」の出演者で、風俗店経営の小栗彩朱佳（あすか）容疑者（31）=名古屋市中区栄2丁目=ら男女3人を風俗営業法違反の疑いで逮捕し、発表した。3人の認否は明らかにしていない。【写真】逮捕された小栗彩朱佳容疑者（中央）=2026年11月15日午前2時26分、愛知県警中署他に逮捕されたのは、職業不詳の大竹宏幸（44）=住居不詳=と風俗店従業員の黒崎真吾（36）=名古屋市東区豊前町2丁目=の両容疑者。県警によると、小栗容疑者と大竹容疑者は、愛知県公安委員会から風俗営業の許可を受けずに、8月15日に名古屋市中区錦3丁目の店舗「guri」で、ボックス席を設け、従業員らに客を接待させ、酒などを提供した疑いがある。黒崎容疑者は11月15日、同様にこの店舗で無許可で風俗営業をした疑いがある。店はショーパブなどの営業に必要な「特定遊興飲食店」の許可を2019年7月に取得していた。この地域では、キャバクラは午前1時までの営業と規制されているが、特定遊興飲食店は午前5～6時を除いて営業が可能となる。県警は、店でショーやダンスなどの提供はなかったとみており、営業時間を長くするために特定遊興飲食店の許可を取っていたとみている。小栗容疑者は、錦三のキャバクラでキャストとして勤務しながら、guriも経営。特定遊興飲食店の許可は小栗容疑者の名前で取得され、黒崎容疑者は店舗責任者を務めていたという。県警は店がキャバクラのアフター用店舗としても使われたとみている。小栗容疑者は名古屋のキャバクラ嬢として知られ、インスタグラムのフォロワー数は80万人を超える。「あっすん」の愛称で、今年8月から配信の「『ラヴ上等』シーズン2」に出演。複数の男女間の恋愛を描いた「恋愛リアリティーショー」として人気を博している。作品内での出演者の発言をめぐり、SNSなどで批判が相次ぎ、法務省は8月、作品とのタイアップポスターの公開中止を発表していた。

title: 公務員が白塗りニンニク姿 体張る
body:
青森県十和田市で2026年5月、白塗りの顔でニンニクに扮した「十和田にんにく娘」がデビューした。市の公式インスタグラムでダンスや行事紹介をするこの4人、実は市職員。日本一のニンニク生産量をうたう市の魅力を体当たりでPRし、反響を呼んでいる。「楽しんで発信する姿を通じ、市の温かさや活気を伝えたい」。目標は真剣そのものだ。（共同通信＝湯山由佳）【写真】宝木を奪い合う男たち「裸祭り」来年は争奪戦せず　岡山の奇祭、参加者2人死亡で
「カ！イ！パ！」。9月末、米寿の市民を祝う会が開かれたホールで、口を大きく開く口腔体操をレクチャーすると、笑い声に包まれた。市内のイベントを中心に今や引っ張りだこだ。ことの始まりは4月。市外で5月半ばに行われる青森のご当地アイドルのライブイベントに向け、シティプロモーション課の係長佐々木教子さん（43）と今泉康将さん（37）は市町村ごとに与えられたPR時間に何を披露するか、知恵を絞っていた。佐々木さんは、市の紹介動画で以前使い、倉庫に置かれたままのニンニクのかぶり物とドーランの存在に気づいた。「今まで通り観光パンフレットを配るだけでは十和田を知ってもらえない。まずはやってみるか」と、今泉さんとニンニク姿になることを決意した。係の別の部下2人に声をかけると「素顔は出したくないけど、白塗りなら…」と承諾。イベント当日、この内1人と今泉さんとを合わせた計3人で登壇した。「ざわっとしたが、受けが良かった」。ライブ会場に出展した市のブースには来場客が殺到した。
「娘」だが佐々木さんは母役。長女役は今泉さん、次女役と8月に合流した三女役は部下だ。デビューと同時に立ち上げた市公式インスタ「十和田市職員の推しごと」には活動の様子を投稿。4人は企画から撮影まで全てをこなす。「内容が堅くならないよう気をつけている」と今泉さん。2026年10月時点でフォロワーは2千人以上、総閲覧数は137万件超と好調だ。ニンニク農家でもある佐々木さんは、自ら変身する意義を「ゆるキャラとは違い、市民の皆さんと話せること」と説く。見た目の強さは市の取り組みを知ってもらう話題づくりに過ぎないと言う。「この熱量を世界にも向けていきたい」。今後は地元企業や農家、学生とのコラボを目指す。

title: 米中露会談 3首脳の思惑が交錯
body: 【ワシントン、北京時事】米中ロ首脳が、史上初となる3カ国首脳会談を開く。既存の国際秩序が揺らぐ中での開催となり、大国の勢力圏分割につながった1945年の米英ソ3首脳による「ヤルタ会談」になぞらえる向きもある。ただ、歴史的な舞台がどれほど内容を伴うかは未知数だ。【ひと目でわかる】米中ロ朝の関係米中は世界1、2位の経済大国。ロシアは言わずと知れた軍事大国で、3カ国とも国連安全保障理事会の常任理事国だ。スウェーデンのストックホルム国際平和研究所（SIPRI）によると、今年1月時点の核弾頭の保有総数はロシアが5420発、米国が5042発、中国が620発で上位3位を占めている。3カ国の首脳が一堂に会する意味は大きく、「米中ロが世界を主導するという図式」（外交関係者）を国際社会に印象付ける可能性がある。トランプ米大統領は、今月3日の米中間選挙で与党共和党が大敗したことから、自身の裁量が大きい外交で「レガシー（政治的遺産）」を残したい意向とされる。ウクライナ侵攻で孤立感が深まるロシアのプーチン大統領には、米中に並ぶ存在感を示す思惑もありそうだ。中国の習近平国家主席にとっても、「大国」としての立場をアピールする機会になる。しかし、米国が議題に挙げる核軍縮や対イラン軍事作戦を巡っては、隔たりがある。トランプ氏は、核戦力を急速に増強する中国を「5、6年でわれわれに追い付くだろう」と警戒。米ロ間の核軍備管理枠組み「新戦略兵器削減条約（新START）」が今年2月に失効したことを受け、3カ国による核軍縮実現に道筋を付けたい考えだ。ロシアは核軍備管理体制の必要性は認めているが、核戦力で米ロに劣る中国は「核軍縮交渉への参加を求められるのは不公平」（中国外務省）と拒否してきた。イラン情勢に関しても、中ロは深入りを避けている。3カ国の利害や思惑は交錯しており、会談の行方は見通せないのが実情だ。

title: 米中露会談 核兵器削減を協議へ
body: 【AFP＝時事】（更新）米ホワイトハウスは13日、ドナルド・トランプ大統領と中国の習近平国家主席、ロシアのウラジーミル・プーチン大統領が来週、中国・深センで開催されるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（APEC）首脳会議に合わせ、異例の米中ロ3か国首脳会談を行うと発表した。【写真】中国は民主派香港紙創業者を「非常に強く憎悪」 トランプ氏、釈放に悲観的ホワイトハウスのオリビア・ウェールズ報道官は、19日に予定されている会談について記者団に対し、「大統領は、世界の核兵器削減を議題の一つとして取り上げる考えを明確にしている。トランプ大統領は、核兵器の拡散は非常に危険だと考えている」と述べた。米政府高官は13日、米中ロ首脳会談ではイラン戦争について協議する一方、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻は議題にならない見通しだと明らかにした。匿名を条件に取材に応じた米政府高官は「トランプ大統領は習近平国家主席、ウラジーミル・プーチン大統領との3者会談で、イランについて話し合う意向だと思う」と述べた。一方、米国はウクライナ政府およびロシア政府と「全く別の枠組み」で交渉を進めていると説明。「中国はその交渉の枠組みに実質的に関与していないため、今回の会談でウクライナ問題を協議するのは適切ではないと思われる」と付け加えた。【翻訳編集】 AFPBB News

title: 米中露首脳会談 19日に中国で開催
body: 米ホワイトハウスは13日、トランプ大統領が中国の習近平（シーチンピン）国家主席、ロシアのプーチン大統領と19日に中国の深圳で会談すると明らかにした。米中ロ3カ国による正式な首脳会談は初めてで、核軍縮などが議題になる見通しとしている。トランプ氏は深圳で18、19両日に開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（APEC）首脳会議に参加する予定で、それに合わせて3カ国会談を行うとの見通しを示していた。プーチン氏も当初から前向きな姿勢を見せていた。会談での議題について、トランプ氏はこれまで核軍備管理などに言及している。ホワイトハウス高官は13日、「大統領は核兵器の拡散が極めて危険だと考えている」と説明し、世界で最も多くの核兵器を持つ3カ国首脳による最初の対話だと強調した。一方、今回の会談では「いかなる合意に至ることも予想していない」と述べ、核軍縮に向けた「出発点」と位置づけた。

title: ウのNATO加盟で東部撤退 米打診
body: ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、ロシアとの和平協議を仲介するアメリカ側から、NATO=北大西洋条約機構への加盟と引き換えに、東部ドンバス地方からの軍の撤退を打診されたと明らかにしました。【写真で見る】「NATO加盟と引き換えにドンバス撤退」アメリカ側がウクライナに初めて打診ウクライナメディアによりますと、ゼレンスキー大統領は13日、アメリカ側から「ウクライナがNATOに加盟する場合、ドンバス地方から軍を撤退させるのか」と問われたことを明らかにしました。ゼレンスキー氏によると、こうした打診を受けるのは初めてで、まだ具体的な情報はないものの、アメリカやNATO加盟国から正式な提案が示された場合には、国民と議論して対応を決める考えを示しました。一方、ロシアはウクライナのNATO加盟を容認しない立場を示しているため、実現性は低いとみられます。ドンバス地方は、ウクライナ東部のドネツク州とルハンシク州からなる地域で、ロシアはドンバス地方全域を掌握するため、侵攻を続けています。ウクライナとロシアの和平協議では東部の領土問題とともに、戦闘終結後の安全の保証などが大きな焦点となっています。

title: 米知事選 民主党が計6州を奪還
body: 【ワシントン共同】米主要メディアは14日、3日投開票のアラスカ州知事選で、民主党新人のジョナサン・クライストムキンズ元州議員が共和党候補3人を破って勝利したと報じた。民主党候補が同州知事選を制したのは1998年以来28年ぶり。これにより中間選挙で実施された36州知事選の勝敗が全て判明。民主党は計6州を奪還し、非改選を含めて計30州を掌握する。高インフレへの不満などを背景にトランプ政権と与党共和党に逆風が吹く中、民主党は中間選挙で連邦議会の上下両院の過半数も握り圧勝した。クライストムキンズ氏は37歳で、12月に就任すれば全米で最年少の現職知事になる。

title: エヌビディアCEO 後任選定難航か
body:
【ニューヨーク共同】米半導体大手エヌビディアの取締役会は13日、不倫騒動で辞任したジェンスン・フアン前最高経営責任者（CEO）の後任選びを本格化した。世界の人工知能（AI）ブームを新たにけん引する役割が期待され、社内外から複数の名前が浮上するものの、新CEOの選定は難航が予想される。【写真】中国企業に買われた「東芝ブランド」その後
英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズによると、エヌビディア取締役会はソフトバンクグループ傘下の英半導体設計大手アームのレネ・ハースCEOに接触した。ハース氏はエヌビディア在籍経験もあり、今もフアン氏や一部役員と親しいとされる。米ブルームバーグ通信は、米同業大手アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシズ（AMD）のリサ・スーCEOも最終候補の1人に残るとみる。エヌビディア社内では、大規模データセンター向け事業を率いるイアン・バック副社長の名が挙がる。AI開発に欠かせないソフトウエア基盤の開発を主導した技術者。ロイター通信によると、金融アナリストや投資家はバック氏と暫定CEOのコレット・クレス氏を有力候補とみる。ただいずれも知名度を欠く。

title: 売れ残りを寄付 広がる一方問題も
body:
“売れ残ったパン”を中心に販売しているサイトを見つけた。その日、残ってしまったパンを冷凍し、一定量が溜まったら購入者に宅配で届ける形で、全国1500店以上のパン屋が参加している。【関連ニュースを動画で】「サブスク福袋」が「食品ロスゼロ」実現の救世主にどんな人気店でも天候などによっては売れ残りがでる。パン屋にとって、廃棄の負担を減らせ、心を込めて作ったパンを守れる取り組みだ。購入者は、自宅にいながら全国のおいしいパンが楽しめ、食品ロスの削減に直接つながる。その上、かなりお得に購入できるとあって、購入待ち数十人という店も珍しくない。そして、サイト運営者は、売り上げの一部を子供の貧困対策へ寄付したり、ロスパンを児童養護施設へ送ったりしているという。「今、このような“社会貢献もできる通販サイト”が増えています」と話すのは、食品流通や流通政策を専門とし、食品ロス削減にも取り組む専修大学商学部の渡辺達朗教授。詳しく聞いた。
【専修大学商学部　渡辺達朗教授】コロナ禍をきっかけに「訳あり商品」を中心に販売する通販サイトが増えました。当時「売りたくても売れない状況」が続き、小売店や外食産業だけでなく、農業者や漁業者も頭を悩ませていました。そんななか、売り損ねて期限が近いものや規格外品といった「訳あり商品」を集めた販売サイトが立ち上がったのです。その後、SDGsの広まりや物価高の影響などもあり「社会貢献もできる通販サイト」という形で広がりを見せています。企業側の「売り切りたい」と、客側の「安く買いたい」に加えて「食品ロスを減らす」「売り上げの一部を寄付する」といった社会貢献の効果もあり、今や定着しつつあります。そして、我々の意識の変化…売れ残りや賞味期限が近い「訳あり商品」に対する価値観が変わり、抵抗なく、むしろ率先して購入するようになってきたことも大きいのではないかと思います。
「食品ロス」が社会問題化したことで、意識して行動されている方も多いと思いますが、取り組む上で注意しなければいけないことがあります。「廃棄の付け替え」です。例えば、消費期限が近い商品が、1つだと100円、3つで200円だったとします。「安いし、たくさん消費した方がいいだろう」と3つを200円で購入したものの、結局、食べきれなかったという経験はありませんか？これだと「事業者の廃棄分が家庭の廃棄に付け替わっただけ」です。また最近は、「レストランで食べ残したものを持ち帰りましょう」という動きが少しずつ広まっています。みなさん、その場では食品ロスや環境のことを考えて持ち帰るのですが、やはり食べきれなかったりする。これもやはり「廃棄の付け替え」で、食品ロスの削減にはなっていません。買い物もレストランでの注文も最初が肝心。「食べきれる分を買う」ことが重要です。今後ますます「計画的な購買行動」が求められる時代になっていくと思います。まずは「賞味期限」と「消費期限」の違いを正しく理解し、「食品ロス」を出さない、無駄のない買い物を目指していただきたいと思います。

title: 月収2万円と年金5万円 70代の現実
body: 「生きるために働く」高齢者。年金だけでは暮らせない中、仕事をしようにも見つからない現実もありました。【写真を見る】月25日働いて手元に残るのは4万円 持病抱え“生きるために働く” 高齢者の現実物価高が直撃する高齢者の暮らし。年金に期待できない中、多くの高齢者が「働かなくてはならない」時代です。（70代男性 Aさん）「千葉でタクシーやっていたんですよ。25年以上やっていた」愛知県一宮市に住む、70代の男性Aさん。（70代男性 Aさん）Q.今は何の仕事をしている?「食料支援の仕事をやっている」Q.ひと月の勤務日数は?「25日くらいですね」■「年金だけではやっていけない」月25日働く70代男性元はタクシードライバーでしたが、交通事故に遭い退職。年金だけでは暮らせず、運送の仕事をしています。（70代男性 Aさん）Q.年金だけではやっていけない?「そうです」この日は市内の病院で、期限切れが近い災害用備蓄品を食料支援の寄付として受け取り、一宮市の福祉支援団体「のわみ相談所」に搬入します。ここでは週に3日、企業や個人から寄付される食料品を生活に困っている人に無償で提供しています。■年金5万円 家賃は3万円で「生活できない」 持病を抱え働き続ける日々報酬は出来高払い。男性自身、ここの食料支援を受けながら運送の仕事もさせてもらっています。毎月の収入は、2万円程度。住んでいるアパートの部屋も、「のわみ相談所」の支援で用意されたもの。ハローワークに何度通っても仕事は見つからず、ここを頼ることになりました。（70代男性 Aさん）「これは厚生年金の通知です」Q.ひと月に年金は?「約5万ですね」Q.家賃は?「3万円（食費込み）です」Q.残り2万では生活できない?「できないです。みんな楽な生活はしていないですよ。だから仕事をやって（ひと月の生活費が）4万円で目いっぱいです」持病のヘルニアを抱えながら、働き続けている男性。（70代男性 Aさん）「我慢して仕事しなければならない。今でも筋肉がすごく痛い」

title: 縦型ショートドラマ トラブル急増
body:
スマートフォンで手軽に視聴でき、幅広い世代に人気が広がる1話1～2分程度の「縦型ショートドラマ」を巡り、サブスクリプション（定額課金）契約を解約できないなどのトラブルが急増していることが14日、共同通信の調査で分かった。2026年9月までの1年間で全国52の消費生活センターに、少なくとも211件の相談が寄せられていた。【画像】突然の通知「５０万円を支払え」、詐欺かと思いきや…ひょっとしてあの動画のせい？ 　放置すれば刑事告訴の恐れも　「便利なソフト」の落とし穴
調査対象は47都道府県と20政令指定都市の消費生活センターで、25年10月～26年9月の1年間を集計した。24年10月～25年9月と比較して相談が「増えている」と答えたのは30自治体で、縦型ドラマの人気とともにこの1年でトラブルが拡大している。「解約方法が分からない」「解約できない」との訴えが46自治体のセンターと最も多く確認された。縦型ショートドラマ市場は中国で急成長し、ここ数年で世界に拡大。情報を集約する国民生活センター（東京）によると、中国語や英語表記のため解約方法が分からなかったり、解約手続きの案内が見つからなかったりする例がある。

title: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
summary: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
body:
Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.
Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment.
The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.
Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days.
Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said.
The US has "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he added.
"It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said.
The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons.
Bryan Bedford, who heads the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), told the same news conference: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI related."
On Saturday L3Harris said it had completed over 70% of the work to modernise communications infrastructure before the shutdown.
"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel," it said in a statement.
"L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously."
'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop
No flights were allowed to take off from the continental US for more than four hours from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday.
More than 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed in the US on Saturday, according to tracking website Flight Aware, as knock-on disruption continues.
In some cases, passengers were left stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to the gates. Some international flights were allowed to depart US airports, in an apparent effort to clear space.
Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure.
US President Donald Trump has requested $30.1bn for the upgrades. Both chambers of Congress are currently controlled by the Republican Party.
Former TSA Administrator John Pistole told the BBC that "the fact that they were able to get it restarted in four-and-a-half hours is good news - it shows a resilience in the system - but what's to say it's not going to happen tomorrow?"
A nationwide ground stop has only been ordered one other time since all flights were banned from take-off for several days following the 11 September 2001 attacks.

title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
summary: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".
body:
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, and a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties".
The Ukrainian leader's comments came after US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a specific proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow.
Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted. It has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.
Other Nato members apart from the US are wary of membership for Ukraine - and it is understood that Ukraine itself sees that as unrealistic.
The Kremlin has always been fiercely opposed, too. It is one reason why Russia started this war in the first place.
It is possible the American envoys were exploring Ukraine's "red lines" when it comes to occupied land in the Donbas. Zelensky said recently that the US mediators believed Kyiv only had to cede territory to achieve peace and were applying pressure, keen to do a deal as soon as possible.
Ukraine is sure that Russia's ambitions are far greater and has long seen Nato as its only sure protection.
So it is also possible that Zelensky made this suggestion public in order to re-open a discussion that had been considered all but closed.
He maintains that the idea is now "back on the agenda" as part of an "extremely difficult conversation" on European security.
It also looks like Ukrainian push-back against Russia's renewed hardline stance. Moscow now talks about a "new European security architecture", which is long-standing Russian code for a weaker Nato.
The issue appears to have been the main focus at the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week.
Hours after Zelensky's remarks, Jared Kushner appeared keen to dampen down any US offer of Nato membership for Ukraine, urging "confidentiality" in a sensitive process.
He said that "maximalist" proposals had been reported from the negotiations, along with "strong political rhetoric".
In what read like a reproach to Kyiv, Kushner referred to "private discussions" aimed at exploring new ideas about ending what he called a "horrible war".
He said the hope was that those ideas might lead to new proposals or breakthroughs.
Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.
It has insisted again that it will not agree to a ceasefire until a final peace deal is in place that would include Ukraine ceding control of those parts of the Donbas Russian troops have not captured, in addition to the Crimean peninsula Moscow annexed illegally in 2014.
The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices.
Zelensky then accused US officials oflimiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service, which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trumpsaid it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president"and called for fresh elections.
Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.

title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
summary: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.
body:
Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670m; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent.
Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.
It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.
The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.
A Meta spokesperson told the BBC that it planned to appeal.
The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts.
Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery.
The regulator said it took into account "the high number of people affected" and the fact it is "still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system".
It also cited "Meta's lack of co-operation".
Meta told the BBC: "We strongly disagree with the [regulator's] assessment of the facts, its application of the law, and the disproportionate level of the fine.
"This is a straightforward feature which helps people post photos and videos to Facebook. People must give permission on their device before it can operate, and they can change this permission at any time via their settings."
Last month, Meta, which is also behind Instagram and WhatsApp, was hit withits largest fine ever for its business practices.
A US judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) after it found that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
summary: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".
body:
SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.
"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.
The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.
But the first catch of the rocket's booster was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday. The booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames just above the sea.
The top part, known as the Ship, returned to Earth a few minutes behind schedule at around 15:20 local time (21:20 GMT) on Saturday, in the first-ever successful catch attempt.

title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
summary: Front-runner Carmelle emerges victorious with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.
body:
Philippines' Carmelle has won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra
The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.
Nineteen-year-old singer Carmelle was always a front runner with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra, complete with its catchy rap section.
She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.
There was a joyous atmosphere at the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheered the contestants and celebrated the popular winner.
Carmelle was the youngest contestant in the competition at 19 years old
Carmelle, the youngest contestant in the competition, was an obvious favourite with the juries and the public despite strong showings from several nations.
Other notable acts included MANG x DAOU, whose emotive duet Aroma elicited huge cheers from the home crowd.
Bangladeshi beatboxers Beatmosphere eschewed the traditional backing track, instead using their voices to replicate the sounds of drums and basslines.
And Laos's Thinla performed her crowd-pleasing song Bae in a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit.
However, the Laotian song had a unintentional second outing after the music video was played over an apparent technical issue during the broadcast - meaning it was the last song the audience heard before the vote.
Thinla wore a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit during her performance
The voting system worked much the same as the European Eurovison, with the public vote accounting for 50% of the result and the other 50% coming from the 11 national juries - with additional points awarded from a rest of the world vote.
Here's how the final scoreboard ended:
1. The Philippines - 211 points
2. Thailand - 170 points
3. Vietnam - 164 points
4. Malaysia - 152 points
6. Bhutan - 126 points
7. Republic of Korea - 113 points
8. Mongolia - 94 points
10. Cambodia - 61 points
11. Bangladesh - 35 points
Also performing during the broadcast was 2026 Eurovision Song Contest winner Dara from Bulgaria, who performed her winning song Bangaranga and new song Bad Idea.
Thai superstar Jeff Satur also made an appearance, hitting the high notes in his performance of Black Tie.
Vietnam's Toc Tien came third with 164 points
Eurovision in Asia was an idea that has been talked about for decades, but one that never seemed to materialise - despite many false starts - until now.
There is a huge enthusiasm here for Eurovision Asia, but a large number of the audience were established fans of the original contest from other countries and regions of the world.
Speaking after the show, fan Zelie Pereira - who travelled from Scotland to Thailand to attend - said she was "very happy" with Carmelle's win.
Eurvosion superfans Michael, Scarlett and Zelie travelled from the UK to Thailand to watch Eurovision Asia's first outing
Korea, Vietnam and Laos also received praise from Pereira and her friends Michael Peters and Scarlett Massie, both from England.
"It was amazing, a very high standard," said Massie.
"The dance was amazing. The sets were amazing. The costumes were amazing. The singing was amazing. Incredible", Peters added.
They confidently declared that "Asia Vision" should be the name for next year's show.
For some, it seems the excitement for another edition is already building.
However the crowd at the One Bangkok Arena thinned out not long after the Philippines singer Carmelle lifted the trophy.
The arena was crowded, but not full, and it's still not clear how much commitment there is among regional broadcasters to keep the contest going and expand it to more than 11 countries.

title: Beauty advent calendars can cost hundreds - but are they value for money?
summary: Beauty calendars have become a Christmas staple and have become particularly popular with female shoppers.
body:
It's easy to see the appeal of a beauty advent calendar. Like many women at this time of year, Julia says she often finds herself tempted to splurge on one - especially a perfume calendar. But she takes quite an unsentimental approach.
"I always look at what's in them. If I like enough of the fragrances, I'll buy it," says the 39-year old, who works as a senior commercial manager in engineering.
Luxury advent calendars are supposed to offer the thrill of a surprise but, for Julia, it is more important she actually wants the items inside - a thought that is also striking more and more customers in the wake of the scandal over the Skims calendar.
Customers likened the contents of Kim Kardashian's Skims calendar to something you would find down the back of a sofa
This week, Kim Kardashian's beauty brandoffered all of its customers refundsfor its $148 (£110) calendar after being widely criticised on social media over the quality of its contents, with some customers likening the hair clips, scrunchies and keychains inside to things you might find down the back of a sofa.
Julia says she earns a good salary but is keen to get value for money and doesn't want to waste it on items she won't use.
"I spent £160 on a Space NK fragrance calendar last year," she says. "I got some fragrances I'd been wanting for a while for a lot less than recommended retail price, and those I didn't like I managed to sell on for a slight mark-up on what I paid."
Julia, 39, says she thinks fragrance calendars are usually good value for money
Beauty calendars, which often cost upwards of £100 and sometimes much more, have been around for more than a decade and the marketing has grown ever more sophisticated.
High-profile brands will warn that their calendars risk running out, which may boost early demand, while unboxing videos posted by influencers can encourage spending by creating an infectious sense of surprise and delight.
And it appears to be working.Ipsos data shows,externalaround 15% of all advent calendars sold are beauty ones, with people aged 18-34 particularly willing to splash out.
But in the face of that tsunami of marketing, customers seem to be getting savvier.
"I love beauty, but I rarely buy beauty advent calendars. They are pricey and often only have a few things that I actually want to try or are trending products," says Priya Raj, 30, a fashion journalist.
She thinks some are good value but, for her, the advantage is being able to try on a small scale without forking out for a full-size product.
"For me, an advent calendar - particularly a beauty one - serves the purpose of allowing me to try out different products, particularly in the lead-up to Christmas, and then I can hopefully snag a bargain in the Boxing Day sales."
Priya Raj, 30, a fashion journalist, says the calendars "serve the purpose of allowing me to try out different products"
Podcaster Rhea Somaiya, 28, also likes the general idea, but has a healthy scepticism around a lot of them in practice.
"I do think some brands take the consumer for granted in that they provide each day with something so menial that people are bombarded with irrelevant and cluttering items.
"And when that's the case, they certainly put me off as the excitement to open each window dwindles into irritation rather than joy."
Podcaster Rhea Somaiya, 28, is less keen on the calendars and says they leave consumers "bombarded with irrelevant and cluttering items"
Jessica Jasper, a marketing consultant, is more positive - she thinks it's worth it. But she also thinks some companies are just jumping on a trend and that "some brands are getting a little carried away with the pricing".
So can beauty calendars offer value for both the brands and the customer - an example of a win-win? Or are they mainly designed to make us spend more at Christmas than we need to?
"Some brands are getting a little carried away with the pricing," says marketing consultant Jessica Jasper
Heather Widdows, a philosophy professor and beauty expert, has pointed out that while you might buy some of the products in an advent calendar individually, it's highly unlikely you'd buyallof them.
"Beauty calendars may offer you lots of products for a really good price. They can also be a bit of fun and feel sensuous.
"But it is exceptionally unlikely that you would use all the products inside them, so they're probably not worth it."
This year, Julia has spent £99 on a John Lewis fragrance calendar which she thinks is good value for money. But it doesn't mean she'll keep everything in it.
In fact she's joined a Facebook group where people trade the ones they don't want for ones they do.
"The ones I keep are already a lot cheaper per mililitre than if you bought them at retail," she says.
With additional reporting from Kris Bramwell

title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
summary: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
body:
A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips.
For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets.
With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years.
Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns.
But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere.
Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips.
Megaspeed is a case in point.
It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.
The city-state has had some success in policing this.
It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places.
They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties.
Megaspeed's office in Singapore
In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore.
The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere.
Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed.
But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department.
Singapore authorities said they had also investigatedAlice Huang- not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud.
In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months.
Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case.
Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing.
In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times.
Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses.
Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity.
On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".
China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following a board meeting
How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness.
In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largelyviews China positively.
For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law.
But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities.
Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case.
BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road.
In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed.
Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man.
During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS.
Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences.
Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government.
Alice Huang, seen here in Taipei with Jensen Huang last year, ran Megaspeed for several months in 2023
All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore.
"For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said.
Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore".
But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips.
With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts.
Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.
Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said.
"Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said.
But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China".
"This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour."
Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit.

title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
summary: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.
body:
Products such as Microsoft Teams and Outlook have been out of service for much of Friday
Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.
The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.
Microsoft apologised for the technical issue, which it said was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not caused by a cyber-attack or an artificial intelligence agent.
Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers.
Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday.
By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, andtrains, hospitals and courts in North America.
Services were beginning to recover by Friday afternoon UK time, nearly 24 hours after the issues first began to emerge.
Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world
In the UK, some parts of the NHS were affected, as were some schools and police forces.
UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls and that there had been no disruption to the transport network.
In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails.
In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook.
Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday.
In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook.
The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals.
Pete says his business has been brought to a standstill
Peter Pentz, a winemaker in South Africa, said his entire business had been effectively brought to a "standstill".
His winery's communication with exports was also brought to a standstill, he said, and "critical production work" had been halted as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations".
Georgia from Staffordshire in England said she had been due to complete her first house purchase after waiting eight months to get to this point - but the outage has delayed that.
"The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies," she said.
"We're not the only one completing today - there are hundreds of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible."
Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally.
It launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, but by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world.
By 13:32, the tech giant said there had been "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region.
Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remained stable once they were up and running again.
"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said.
"We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously."
A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review.
Experts said that while workers may have been happy to not have email access for a working day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services.
"The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure.
Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem.
"Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said.
"In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur."

title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
summary: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
body:
Watch: What we know so far about the Microsoft outage
A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world.
Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced.
Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption.
Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong.
Schools, GPs and businesses hit by global Microsoft outage as company scrambles to solve issue
Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries.
From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps.
But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues.
As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America.
The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues".
In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels".
The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.
"We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday.
Although services are beginning to resume, Microsoft has warned of continued "intermittent access issues", meaning some users will still struggle to load their inboxes and could experience "delayed email delivery".
In other words, it is not quite safe to assume every email you send is going to arrive in its intended recipient's inbox right away.
Earlier, Microsoft said it would be extending the "timeout window" to 48 hours "to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up".
The email timeout window refers to the amount of time Outlook will wait to receive an email.
When they do show up, the timestamp will be when they were delivered rather than when they were sent.
Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time.
Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues.
"What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said.
"The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs.
"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in.
"You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit."
The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online.
Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time".
He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal.
Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.
"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.
"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.
In a statement, Microsoft said it was "deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners.
"We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services."
More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed.
Microsoft 365 is used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services.
Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic both earlier reported problems as a result of the outage.
ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which had caused some tools to not work as expected.
From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies,disruption across the globe has been widespread.
Courts from Los Angeles to Texas earlier warned that communications might be delayed.
In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected.
The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.
Across the UK,GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage.
Some GP surgeries had urged patients not to submit messages via their website while police forces were also earlier asking the public to call if they want to make a report.

title: Pressure grows on Trump's Commerce Secretary Lutnick in fallout from Nvidia scandal
summary: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
body:
How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.
Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.
Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.
Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but was not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with.
Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.
Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said some parts of the administration wanted more controls on trade with Megaspeed
Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.
"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.
Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.
There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but the Financial Times separately reported that the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.
However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia.
"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," hetold CNBC,external.
"The real story here should be: did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?
"It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that."
Bessent's pointed comments are a rare instance of internal debate within the Trump administration spilling out into the public view, although tensions have reportedly simmered between Bessent and Lutnick in the past.
In 2024, the two reportedly jostled for the role of treasury secretary ahead of Trump's return to the White House, and last year the pair butted heads over the administration's tariff policy, according to US media.
How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
Huang has beensummoned to testifybefore the Senate Banking Committee about his alleged affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.
The commerce secretary has also been summoned to appear before the committee in December.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," committee chairman Republican Senator Tim Scott posted on X.
Democrats on key congressional committees have asked the Commerce Department and Lutnick to keep all records relating to decisions to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, including all their communications with or about Nvidia and Huang.
Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden are starting investigations into the way Nvidia was allowed to sell these chips.
They say Nvidia's advanced H200 chips could be sold to Chinese firms if they were first imported from their manufacturing facility in Taiwan into the US for inspection.
A 25% tariff - a levy paid by US importers to the federal government - was imposed on those chips under a section of the Trade Act that Neal and Wyden say is meant to allow the US president to take action against imports that risk national security.
"Trump's use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk," they said.

title: Young people should have legal guarantee of job or training, Milburn tells BBC
summary: The author of a major review on youth unemployment, due next week, acknowledges the change would mean some young people losing out on benefits.
body:
Young people should have a legal guarantee to a job or training, Milburn says
Young people should have a legal guarantee of a job, training or employment support, the author of a major review of youth unemployment has told the BBC.
Alan Milburn, the former Labour minister whose proposals on welfare and young people will be unveiled on Tuesday, said those who refuse to take up the help could lose their benefits.
In an interview to be broadcast on Sunday, Milburn called for a radical shift in government spending away from benefits for young people to measures that support them into work.
He claims the government spends25 times as much on benefits for young people than it spends on supporting them into employment, and believes the ratio should shift to two to one.
That would mean significant cuts to benefit spending and significant extra taxpayers' cash for training, education or other forms of support.
Milburn said "the pendulum's swung far too far from the one to the other - £25 to one, and we can take everything to £2 to one".
He added: "To do that, we've got to invest, less in benefits, so we've got to be paying out less in benefits."
The former MP acknowledged that would mean some young people losing out on benefits, arguing the system should focus on helping people into work rather than keeping them dependent on welfare.
Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?
Milburn said the government is already spending £22bn a year supporting young people who are economically inactive, and that money needs to be spent differently.
He has already said that the under 25s should no longer be able to claim some health benefits – the personal independence payment and the health element of Universal Credit.
In his other major announcement, Milburn spoke of the proposal he calls an "opportunity guarantee" for young people.
This would put a legal duty on government to ensure young people have access to a route into employment.
He said: "It should be a guarantee for a young person. Because at the moment the only guarantee they've got is a very simple thing. To get a benefit. What sort of life is that?"
The "opportunity guarantee" might work similarly to the way that councils have a legal responsibility to offer homeless people accommodation or advice, or accommodate children in care.
Milburn argues previous employment schemes have been temporary, and says a permanent legal entitlement is needed to tackle the long-running problem of young people not in education, employment or training.
The government is expected broadly to welcome the proposals, which will be published in full on Tuesday, with a statement in Parliament and draft laws early next year.
Almost one million young people in the UK are not in employment, education or training - otherwise known as Neet -according to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described Milburn's forthcoming report as a "watershed moment," but stopped short of committing to implementing its recommendations in full.
Burnham also insisted paying for the reforms would not mean "more money" but "spending differently" in government when pressed on the large upfront investment they are expected to require.
Asked whether he would accept the politically sensitive report in full, Burnham declined to provide that "blanket assurance".
Speaking at the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday, Burnham said that the report addressed the "youth detachment" that has been on the rise since the pandemic.
"It can't be right that we've stripped away support from young people as a society, as life is getting harder for them and growing up is getting more difficult," he said.
The prime minister added that the government was also looking at a new vision for schooling that is "not focused solely on the university route" and which offerstechnical education alongside traditional academic learning.
Lord Blunkett, a former Labour home secretary, told the BBC that money from cutting benefits spending should be reassigned to supporting employment "at least in the immediate future".
Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, he said reforms should focus on "transferring resource that currently goes into paying for failure, keeping youngsters at home, isolated, lonely, into actually putting the money in and the resource and the commitment in to making those jobs available".
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has previously said the government should not be spending "lots of time" on employment schemes, which she said would ultimately fail.
Her party and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence.
Reform economy spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "This review is pointless unless we get action from Burnham straight away.
"It cannot be right that this continues for another 10 years before the youth benefits bill comes down."
Green Party leader Zack Polanski said it was "disappointing" the Milburn review had "come up with the same tired conclusions" on youth unemployment.
Polanski added: "Using benefit sanctions to force young people into low-paid, insecure work doesn't solve the structural inequalities they face, and it deepens poverty."
The Liberal Democrats want the government to introduce a 100-hour work experience guarantee and a careers coach for every young person.
They believe this would equip youngsters with the best possible skills before they leave school.
The TUC - the umbrella group for unions in the UK - welcomed Milburn's proposal of a legal guarantee as a "game changer", describing the country's number of Neets as a "national emergency".
But it stressed that funding for additional support for young people should not come from public service budgets. "In further education, funding needs to be targeted at the workforce, as well as provision, to tackle the recruitment and retention crisis and massive pay disparities in the sector," it said.
"A zero sum approach would be wrong and counter-productive."

title: UK ethics watchdog chief steps back from role over sexual misconduct claims
summary: The government says Stuart Sterling has stepped back from his role after claims made during the early 2000s emerged.
body:
Stuart Sterling was appointed chief executive of the Ethics and Integrity Commission last year
The head of the government's main ethics watchdog has stepped back after it emerged he was investigated in a previous job over alleged sexual misconduct involving female colleagues, and had, in one case, been sanctioned.
Stuart Sterling was appointed as the first chief executive of the newly formed Ethics and Integrity Commission in October 2025.
The existence of the allegations against Sterling, and the investigations into them, were first reported by the Sunday Times.
Following the report, a government spokesperson said: "These are serious allegations. Stuart Sterling has stepped back from his role while we swiftly establish the facts."
The Labour Party promised in its 2024 manifesto to create the commission to "ensure probity in government" in response to scandals during the Covid pandemic.
As its head, Sterling's role included advising the prime minister on tackling misconduct in public life.
The Sunday Times reported that, in 2003, Sterling had been subject to a "full misconduct hearing" when he was a junior officer with Northamptonshire Police in what was treated as a case "of sexual harassment".
The paper said he had been accused of inappropriately touching the breasts of a female colleague in a police station, and a male colleague who allegedly witnessed the event had reported him to his superiors. It reported that he had been suspended on full pay.
A representative for Mr Sterling said: "Stuart states that a full disciplinary process was held regarding the complaint in 2002. He complied with this fully. It resulted in a sanction."
The Sunday Times reported that he was given a financial penalty of two weeks' pay. It said that, at the time, that was the maximum sanction possible short of forced resignation. He then received two police commendations and was promoted to be a detective sergeant.
The Sunday Times said that by 2008 Mr Sterling had been reported to the force again after another allegation of sexual misconduct against a female colleague, this time at a social gathering outside work.
Mr Sterling's representative said: "He denies that the alleged incident in 2008 ever took place. He was never subject to any criminal investigation, but the allegation was examined by professional standards".
The representative added: "He was not required to resign from the force. He left voluntarily".
Northamptonshire Police has confirmed that it holds a digital record of a misconduct process from 2002.
It did not comment on the later allegation.
In 2009, Sterling joined the Cabinet Office. It is not clear what vetting process he underwent. He has since served in a variety of senior roles and in 2019 was seconded to the National Police Chiefs' Council. In 2023 he received an OBE for helping to plan the funeral of Queen Elizabeth.
It is understood the Cabinet Office will now examine whether appropriate and correct disclosures of information were made.

title: Reform and Tory spokesmen in angry clash over immigration at Piddington
summary: Reform's Zia Yusuf and Tory Chris Philp were speaking against converting a former military site into asylum accommodation.
body:
Watch: Philp and Yusuf have public clash over immigration
Conservative MP Chris Philp and Reform UK's Zia Yusuf had a blazing row at a joint press conference, as they joined villagers protesting against asylum accommodation plans.
The pair clashed when sharing a platform in Piddington to oppose converting a former military site at MoD Bicester into accommodation for more than 1,200 detained asylum seekers.
The two politicians were invited to make speeches about the plans, but things became heated after Yusuf asked Philp to apologise for the Conservatives' record on immigration.
Philp, the shadow home secretary, told Yusuf to "calm down" and accused him of "cheap politics", an assertion Reform's home affairs spokesman dismissed.
Asylum centre on military base near Piddington approved
A press conference led by Piddington Parish Council chairman Tim McNally took place on Friday after Housing Secretary Angela Rayner approved the Home Office's application to change the use of the site for asylum accommodation.
The Home Office said this would allow it to continue developing the plan but that no final decision on the site had been taken.
There has been significant local opposition to the proposal and a legal challenge to the planning decision is expected from the parish council.
In September,Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UKover the planned use for the site in Oxfordshire.
Politicians from the Conservatives and Reform have made several visits to Piddington, a village of about 350 people, to show their support for campaigners.
Speaking on Friday, Philp said a future Conservative government would shut the asylum accommodation "straight away" if it was opened by Labour.
Yusuf made clear Reform's opposition to the plans before his focus switched to the Conservatives.
He said: "It's obviously true that we would not be gathered here today and 1,200 men would not be being dumped into this beautiful village were it not for the actions of the Conservative government.
"So I actually want to ask you Chris, would you actually like to apologise for the things you did in government to bring hundreds of thousands of people into this country illegally?"
Philp, a former immigration minister, described Yusuf's remarks as "disingenuous" and argued the migrants who could be housed near Piddington will have arrived in the country while Labour has been in power.
He said the Conservatives are under new leadership and he hoped the politicians could "stand in solidarity with the residents" rather than "engage in point scoring".
Philp added: "Zia, read the room, listen to the people clapping and read the room."
Yusuf countered that it was "important that we hold everybody accountable for this situation" and said Philp had been "heavily involved in immigration and borders policy" for the Conservatives in government.
Philp repeated his "read the room" suggestion, adding: "The public here want you to pipe down on the cheap politics."
Yusuf dismissed the suggestion that he was engaging in "cheap politics" and repeated his criticism of the Conservatives' record, saying they "refused" to secure the country's borders when in power.
As Yusuf spoke, Philp could be heard saying: "Buddy, I'm not here to give you comms advice, mate, you're in a hole stop digging."
Philp told Yusuf he should "calm down", with the Reform politician repeating his request for the Conservative MP to "apologise to the British people".
McNally thanked the pair for attending the press conference, adding: "I understand this is a passionate discussion and I respect you both for what you've got to do and what you represent."
While the two parties are on the right of politics, it is unusual for them to share a platform to campaign and both are keen to stress their differences to voters.
Reform leader Nigel Farage has pitched the party asreplacing the "old, fuddy-duddy" Conservatives, and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has said she wouldrather have another general electionthan do a deal with Reform to secure power.
Up to 1,256 men could be housed at the site near Bicester under the plans
Government ministers want to use former military bases as part of efforts close all asylum hotels.
Insisting that the MoD Bicester accommodation will be safe, the prime minister's deputy spokeswoman said such sites are "designed to be self-contained with 24/7 security and CCTV to minimise the impact on the local community".
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also previously said it shouldnot just be the poorest communitiesreceiving dispersed refugees and asylum seekers.
Liberal Democrat MP Calum Miller told the BBC he was "very disappointed" but not "surprised" by the government's decision to grant planning permission.
Miller, whose constituency of Bicester and Woodstock includes the military site, said "the government was marking the government's application".
He said the decision "lays bare the weakness of the application and the many, many problems with it, because this is not a suitable site and it is not the right place to put a large-scale asylum centre".
